stage1_evidence_shown.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To determine if temperature during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) has an effect on perioperative and postoperative thyroid function.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: DESIGN
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Prospective study comparing thyroid function during and after hypothermic and normothermic CPB.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: SETTING
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Cardiac surgical unit at a university-affiliated hospital.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: PATIENTS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Twelve patients scheduled to undergo cardiac operations with normothermic (n = 6) or hypothermic (n = 6) CPB.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: INTERVENTIONS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Blood was analyzed for serum concentration of total thyroxine (TT4), total triiodothyronine (TT3), free T3 (fT3), reverse T3 (rT3), and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) preoperatively, 60 min after CPB was initiated, 30 min after discontinuing CPB, and on postoperative days (POD) 1, 3, and 5.

stage2_added_evidence.label: MEASUREMENTS AND RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: Patients who underwent either cold (26 degrees +/- 5 degrees C) or warm (35 degrees +/- 1 degree C) CPB were comparable with regard to age, body weight, duration of CPB, cross-clamp time, use of inotropes, total heparin dose, and length of hospital stay. Incidence of postoperative myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, and death were similar. In both groups, TT4 and TT3 were reduced below baseline values beginning with CPB and persisting for up to 5 days after CPB (p<0.05), free T3 was reduced for up to 3 days after CPB (p<0.05), mean serum rT3 was elevated on POD 1 and POD 3 (p<0.05), and TSH remained unchanged.
